target.title: security: deny-all top-level token permissions on release workflows; maintainer-skill temp-file hygiene
target.body:
## Summary

Security hardening in three small pieces, all metadata/docs-only (no runtime code):

1. **Top-level `permissions: {}` on the 6 release workflows** (`docker-release`, `macos-release`, `openclaw-npm-release`, `openclaw-release-checks`, `plugin-clawhub-release`, `plugin-npm-release`). Audited every job in all six workflows: each already declares its own job-level `permissions`, so the implicitly permissive workflow-default `GITHUB_TOKEN` was unused attack surface. Deny-all at the top level makes the job-level declarations the single source of truth.
2. **GHSA maintainer skill — temp-file hygiene**: the documented pattern used fixed, predictable `/tmp/ghsa.*` paths for pre-publish advisory drafts (sensitive until published). Now uses `mktemp -d` + a cleanup `trap`. Also fixes the verify example, which read `/tmp/ghsa.refetch.json` without any step ever writing that file — it now captures the `gh api` refetch into a variable and checks `state`/`published_at`/escaped-newline in one pass. Follow-up (ClawSweeper P2 + two defects found while reproducing it): the escaped-newline check now gates explicitly with `if … rg -q …` printing `FAIL`/`PASS` instead of leaving the bare `rg` exit as the result (rg exits 0 exactly when the forbidden literal `\n` is present, so the bad state looked like the passing path); the pattern is now `rg '\\n'` (the previous `rg '\\\\n'` matched two backslashes + `n` and never matched the guarded sample); and the snippet uses `printf '%s'` instead of `echo` (zsh/dash `echo` rewrites backslash escapes, turning the JSON's escaped backslash-n into a real newline before jq/rg see it — hiding the very thing the check guards).
3. **Secret-scanning maintainer skill**: the Step 7 example used a fixed `/tmp/results.json`, contradicting the skill's own "mktemp with random UUIDs for all temp files" rule — now uses a `mktemp -d` work dir. The commit-leak section previously said only "Cannot clean. Notify author…"; it now includes context gathering (is the commit on an open PR?) and situation-matched remediation templates (amend for the latest commit, rebase for an older one, escalate-without-force-push-instructions when merged to the default branch).

Deliberately **not** included (evaluated and dropped):

- Wiring `lint:tmp:dynamic-import-warts` into the CI boundary checks: the script is advisory-by-default and the tree currently has 4 outstanding findings (matrix, qa-lab, qa-matrix, qqbot), so gating it is a separate ratcheting effort.
- Migrating `extensions/acpx/index.ts` to `definePluginEntry()`: 48 of 139 bundled entries still use the plain-object pattern, so a single-plugin migration is churn, not a completion.

## Verification

Metadata/docs-only change; validated with the light path:

- `git diff --check` — clean.
- YAML parse + semantic assert on all 6 workflows (`permissions` parses to `{}` at top level, `jobs` intact).
- Per-job permissions audit: every job in all 6 workflows declares job-level `permissions`, so deny-all cannot strip a permission any job relies on.
- `oxfmt --check` on all 8 changed files — clean (repo-wide `pnpm format:check` fails on 193 pre-existing files on current `main`, unrelated to this change).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Implicitly permissive workflow-default `GITHUB_TOKEN` on the 6 release workflows; predictable fixed `/tmp` temp paths plus a verify example that read a never-written file in the GHSA and secret-scanning maintainer skills.
Real environment tested: Local source checkout on top of `openclaw/openclaw@2ba622ca301` (macOS, Node 25, pnpm 11.2.2). The change is CI metadata + skill docs only; no app runtime surface exists to exercise.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git diff --check`; YAML parse + assert of all 6 workflows (top-level `permissions` parses to `{}` and `jobs` intact) via `node` with the repo's yaml package; awk audit listing every job and its job-level `permissions` block in all 6 workflows; `npx oxfmt --check` on all 8 changed files; verifier probe: two synthetic advisory JSON fixtures built with `jq -n` (one whose description contains a literal escaped `\n`, one with only a real newline) run through the exact documented snippet (with `gh api` substituted by `cat fixture`) under zsh.
Evidence after fix: All 6 workflows parse clean with top-level `permissions: {}`; the per-job audit shows every job (5+1+3+16+6+5) declares its own `permissions`, so deny-all cannot strip a permission any job uses; oxfmt reports all 8 files format-clean; the fixed verifier prints `FAIL: description contains a literal escaped \n` on the bad fixture and `PASS: description clean` on the clean one (the prior snippet printed nothing on the bad fixture and exited 0).
Observed result after fix: No behavior change to any runtime path; release workflows keep their explicit job-level grants and lose only the unused implicit default token scope.
What was not tested: An actual release-workflow run under the deny-all default (release workflows are maintainer-triggered tag/dispatch flows; the per-job permissions audit above is the safety argument). The skill markdown changes are operator documentation and were not executed end-to-end against a live advisory/alert.
